function.name: career_application_create
function.description: Saves a job posting (or an application) to the user's career tracker. Hominem does not fetch job sites: read the posting yourself, then pass what you found. Include company and title exactly as posted, the posting URL, the full posting text in postingText, the posted pay range in salaryMin/salaryMax/salaryCurrency, and the board's own job id in externalId with the board name in source when the page shows one. Leave out anything the posting does not say; only company and title are required, so do not ask the user for the rest. Saving the same posting twice is harmless because repeats are detected. New postings default to the WISHLIST status. If the user already saved this posting the tool creates nothing and returns the existing record with alreadyExisted true; check its title and company match before telling the user it was saved. Mode: write.

company.description: Company name exactly as the posting shows it.

title.description: Job title exactly as the posting shows it.

location.description: Location as posted, e.g. "San Francisco, CA" or "Remote (US)". Omit if unknown.

source.description: Where the posting lives: the job board or ATS, e.g. "Ashby", "Greenhouse", "LinkedIn".

jobPostingUrl.description: Link to the posting. Tracking params like utm_* are ignored when checking for duplicates; keep any job-id param.

externalId.description: The job board's own id for the posting (JSON-LD identifier, Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby job id) when the page exposes one. With source, this is the strongest duplicate check.

postedAt.description: Date the posting went up, YYYY-MM-DD.

postingText.description: The full posting body as plain text. Read the page yourself and paste it; do not summarize.

salaryMin.description: Bottom of the posted pay range in whole currency units per year. Omit if not posted.

salaryMax.description: Top of the posted pay range in whole currency units per year. Omit if not posted.

salaryCurrency.description: ISO currency code for the posted range, e.g. "USD".

salaryExpectation.description: What the user hopes to earn, in whole currency units per year, like salaryMin and salaryMax. For the pay range in the posting use salaryMin and salaryMax instead.

notes.description: The user's own notes, not the posting text.

Do not use when: Do not invent an application id or delete before lookup and confirmation.  Prerequisites: career_applications (resolve the stable application id).

company.description: Company name exactly as the posting shows it.

title.description: Job title exactly as the posting shows it.

location.description: Location as posted, e.g. "San Francisco, CA" or "Remote (US)". Omit if unknown.

source.description: Where the posting lives: the job board or ATS, e.g. "Ashby", "Greenhouse", "LinkedIn".

jobPostingUrl.description: Link to the posting. Tracking params like utm_* are ignored when checking for duplicates; keep any job-id param.

externalId.description: The job board's own id for the posting (JSON-LD identifier, Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby job id) when the page exposes one. With source, this is the strongest duplicate check.

postedAt.description: Date the posting went up, YYYY-MM-DD.

postingText.description: The full posting body as plain text. Read the page yourself and paste it; do not summarize.

salaryMin.description: Bottom of the posted pay range in whole currency units per year. Omit if not posted.

salaryMax.description: Top of the posted pay range in whole currency units per year. Omit if not posted.

salaryCurrency.description: ISO currency code for the posted range, e.g. "USD".

salaryExpectation.description: What the user hopes to earn, in whole currency units per year, like salaryMin and salaryMax. For the pay range in the posting use salaryMin and salaryMax instead.

notes.description: The user's own notes, not the posting text.

function.name: career_worklog_create
function.description: Records a career worklog entry. Only the engagement and the raw note are required; every other field can be filled in later by updating the entry. Mode: write. Use when: The user reports work they just did, or work worth keeping a record of. Do not use when: Do not use to edit an existing entry; use career_worklog_update.  Prerequisites: career_engagements (resolve the engagement the work belongs to).  Produces: worklog entry id.

engagementId.description: The engagement this work belongs to; it must be the caller’s own.

rawNote.description: The user’s words, verbatim. Captured once and never rewritten.

occurredStart.description: Start of the work window (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to the create date.

occurredEnd.description: End of the work window (YYYY-MM-DD). Must be on or after occurredStart; null is a single day or an ongoing window.

area.description: System or surface the work touched.

problem.description: What was broken, risky, or missing.

action.description: What the user did — the mechanism.

impact.description: The outcome, with a metric when known.

impactStatus.description: `open` (default) while the outcome is unknown; `closed` once it is known.

tags.description: Free-form labels. Defaults to an empty list.

sensitivity.description: Guidance for downstream consumers, not access control. Defaults to `internal`.

evidence.description: Light pointers to backing artifacts. Replaced wholesale on update.

function.name: career_worklog_delete
function.description: Deletes a career worklog entry. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: A matching worklog entry id has been returned by career_worklog_entries. Do not use when: Do not invent an entry id or delete before lookup and confirmation.  Prerequisites: career_worklog_entries (resolve the stable entry id).

function.name: career_worklog_entries
function.description: Lists career worklog entries — the record of work as it happened — newest first. Filters combine, and each one narrows the result further. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks what they worked on, when, and what it changed. Do not use when: Do not use for the static career layer (engagements, projects, skills); those have their own tools.  Produces: worklog entry ids.

projectId.description: Only entries linked to this project.

skillId.description: Only entries that prove this skill, as linked from the skill’s worklogEntryIds.

impactStatus.description: `open` is the follow-up queue: the outcome is still unknown.

tag.description: Only entries carrying exactly this tag.

occurredAfter.description: Inclusive lower bound on the entry’s start date (YYYY-MM-DD).

occurredBefore.description: Inclusive upper bound on the entry’s start date (YYYY-MM-DD).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return, from 1 to 100.

function.name: career_worklog_entry
function.description: Returns one career worklog entry with the skills that point at it. The raw note is the user’s words, captured once. Mode: read-only. Use when: One specific worklog entry has been resolved by id. Do not use when: Do not use when a list answers the question; use career_worklog_entries.  Prerequisites: career_worklog_entries (resolve the stable entry id).

function.name: career_worklog_update
function.description: Updates a career worklog entry. The raw note, the capture time, and the id are immutable once the entry exists. Mode: write. Use when: An entry id has been returned by career_worklog_entries. Do not use when: Do not try to rewrite the raw note, the capture time, or the id — they cannot change after creation.  Prerequisites: career_worklog_entries (resolve the stable entry id).

function.name: collection_detail
function.description: Get a collection's details, items, and members. Mode: read-only.

function.name: container_create
function.description: Creates a container, optionally nested inside another via parentContainerId. Check container_list first to avoid duplicates. Mode: write.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).  Produces: id.

function.name: container_delete
function.description: Deletes a container. Possessions and child containers inside it are NOT deleted: they become unplaced / top-level. Mode: write, confirmation required. Do not use when: Do not delete before lookup and confirmation.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).

function.name: container_get
function.description: Returns a container with its direct child containers and the possessions inside it (each capped at 100; totalChildren / totalPossessions give the full counts, archived possessions included). When a total exceeds what was returned, page with container_list (parentContainerId) or possession_list (containerId) using offset. container is null if it does not exist. Mode: read-only. Use when: Asking "what is in X" or "what is inside this box". Do not use when: Do not invent a container id.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).

function.name: container_list
function.description: Lists containers (boxes, rooms, shelves, bags) ordered by name, each with its parent container id and a count of non-archived possessions inside. The nesting tree can be rebuilt from parentContainerId. Pages of up to 100: use offset to continue, query to match a name, or parentContainerId to list one container's direct children. Mode: read-only. Use when: Resolving a container id or seeing how things are organized.  Produces: id.

function.name: container_move
function.description: Nests a container inside another (parentContainerId) or makes it top-level (null). Cycles are rejected. Returns null if the container does not exist. Mode: write. Use when: Re-organizing the container hierarchy.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).

function.name: container_update
function.description: Updates fields on a container. Only provided fields change; metadata keys are merged. Returns null if the container does not exist. Re-parenting that would nest a container inside itself or its own contents is rejected. Mode: write. Use when: A container id has been returned by container_list or container_get. Do not use when: Do not invent a container id.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).

function.name: container_upsert
function.description: Creates a container or updates the one already carrying externalId (e.g. CON-023). Returns the id and whether the row was created. Re-running with the same input never duplicates. Mode: write. Use when: Importing or syncing a container that has a stable external id.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).  Produces: id.

function.name: create_collection
function.description: Create a new collection for grouping any supported entities. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: The user explicitly requests a new collection and no matching collection exists. Do not use when: Do not create duplicate collections or execute before confirmation.  Produces: collection id, collection name.

visibility.description: Whether collaborators can access the collection.

function.name: decline_collection_invite
function.description: Declines the caller's pending invitation to collaborate on a collection. Mode: write, confirmation required. Prerequisites: list_pending_collection_invites (resolve the pending invite).

function.name: delete_collection
function.description: Permanently deletes a collection you own, along with its membership list. The items in it are not deleted. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: The user explicitly asks to delete a collection they own. Do not use when: Do not delete without confirmation, and do not use it to leave a shared one.  Prerequisites: list_collections (resolve the stable collection id).

function.name: entity_tags
function.description: Lists tags assigned to an owned person, venue place, possession, note, or travel entity, including a Residence. Mode: read-only.

function.name: finance_account_create
function.description: Create a finance account, or return the existing one when the name matches case-insensitively (created: false). Accounts created here are what sheet imports resolve against; the import never auto-creates an unknown account. includeInNetWorth defaults to true; an existing account keeps its stored value. dryRun reports the outcome without writing. Mode: write. Use when: A sheet label or sync source needs an account that does not exist yet. Do not use when: Do not use to rename, close, or merge an existing account.  Produces: account ids, account names.

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. USD or GBP.

allowedCurrencies.description: Currencies this account can hold; currencyCode is always allowed.

accountNumber.description: Mask / last digits as displayed elsewhere.

accountType.description: Account type; cash/checking/savings count as liquid in finance_runway, so pick it deliberately.

includeInNetWorth.description: Whether the account counts toward finance_net_worth totals. Defaults to true.

function.name: finance_account_delete
function.description: Permanently delete an empty account by id. Accounts with transactions cannot be deleted. The MCP server asks for confirmation before deletion. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: Removing an empty test or duplicate account permanently. Do not use when: Do not delete an account with transactions; move or delete those first.  Prerequisites: finance_account_summary (verify the account is empty).

accountId.description: Stable account id returned by a Finance tool.

function.name: finance_account_summary
function.description: Reconcile per account: transaction and excluded counts, per-currency totals, and the posted-on span. Counts and totals cover every row (pending and excluded included), and closed accounts are included by default. Mode: read-only. Use when: Verifying an import or reconciling account totals without paging transactions. Do not use when: Do not use for spending breakdowns; use finance_spending_by_category.  Produces: per-account transaction counts, per-account totals.

accountId.description: Restrict to a single account; omit to summarize every account.

includeClosed.description: Include closed accounts (default true — reconciliation must see everything).

function.name: finance_account_update
function.description: Partially update an account addressed by id: name, institution, accountNumber (mask), accountType, status, allowedCurrencies and includeInNetWorth. Omitted fields are unchanged; null clears institution/accountNumber. Identity — id, transactions, links — never changes, and currencyCode is immutable here. includeInNetWorth is independent of status. dryRun projects the change set without applying it. Mode: write. Use when: Correcting account metadata or changing the currencies allowed for its transactions. Do not use when: Do not use to change an account currency (immutable) or to delete/merge accounts (out of scope).  Prerequisites: finance_accounts (resolve the account id).

accountId.description: Stable account id — names are mutable, so updates address by id, never by name.

name.description: New display name; must stay unique per owner (case-insensitive).

accountNumber.description: Mask / last digits; null clears it.

currencyCode.description: Immutable through this tool — any change is refused with currency_immutable.

allowedCurrencies.description: Full set of currencies this account may hold; currencyCode is always included.

includeInNetWorth.description: Whether the account counts toward finance_net_worth totals. Omit to leave it unchanged; independent of status.

dryRun.description: Project the change set without applying it.

function.name: finance_accounts
function.description: List finance accounts with type, currency, lifecycle status and current balance (posted transactions only). Unlike finance_net_worth this includes accounts left out of net-worth totals, such as credit cards. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks which accounts they have, or an account id is needed as a filter. Do not use when: Do not use for net worth totals; use finance_net_worth.  Produces: account ids, account names, account balances.

function.name: finance_budget_breakdown
function.description: Split a monthly income into a 50/30/20 needs, wants and savings budget. Pure calculation over the given income; reads no ledger data. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks how to budget a given income. Do not use when: Do not use to report what the user actually spent.  Produces: needs allocation, wants allocation, savings allocation.

savingsTargetCents.description: Desired monthly savings in cents. Capped at 20% of income.

function.name: finance_categories
function.description: List finance categories (id, name) for the authenticated user. Use to resolve sheet Category names before import. Mode: read-only.

function.name: finance_category_create
function.description: Create a finance category, or return the existing one when the name matches case-insensitively (created: false). Categories are what the sheet import resolves against and what budgets reference. dryRun reports the outcome without writing. Mode: write.

function.name: finance_category_delete
function.description: Permanently delete an unused category by name or id. Categories referenced by transactions and Uncategorized cannot be deleted. The MCP server asks for confirmation before deletion. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: Removing an unused test or duplicate category permanently. Do not use when: Merge a category first if its transactions should be kept.  Prerequisites: finance_categories (resolve the category by name or id).

function.name: finance_category_merge
function.description: Merge one or more categories into a target in three ordered stages: preserve (a tag naming each source is put on its transactions), repoint (automation rules filing into a source are rewritten to the target), merge (transactions move and the sources are removed). Uncategorized may be a target, never a source. Any rule that still names a source blocks the merge and is listed by name, and so does a source whose transactions are not yet tagged. stage runs all three stages by default, or one at a time. dryRun reports all three stages without writing. Mode: write, confirmation required.

from.description: One or more categories to fold away, by name or id.

into.description: Category to keep, by name or id.

stage.description: Which stage of the ordered flow to run: all (default, preserve → repoint → merge in one transaction), or a single stage so the ordering can be driven step by step. The merge stage refuses if a source is untagged or a rule still names one.

dryRun.description: Report all three stages without writing.

function.name: finance_category_tag_breakdown
function.description: Drill into one category: its spending grouped by tag over a date range (defaults to the last 30 days through today), with each tag bucket and the category totals reported per currency. Tags are the layer beneath categories, so this is how a merged category is split back into the components it absorbed. Check warnings: tag buckets overlap when a transaction carries more than one tag. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks what a category is made of, or which components drive its total. Do not use when: Use finance_spending_by_category for the category totals themselves.  Prerequisites: finance_categories (resolve the category by name or id).  Produces: tag names, per-tag spending, per-tag transaction counts.

category.description: Category name or id to drill into.

from.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD); defaults to 30 days ago.

to.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD); defaults to today.

function.name: finance_monthly_stats
function.description: Summarize posted, non-excluded activity for one month by currency: income, expenses, net, transaction count, top tag and top merchant. Mixed-currency months return null for combined monetary values and include currencyBreakdown. Computed from posted, non-excluded transactions in the range. Spending is every negative amount, so transfers between accounts are included. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks how a month went financially. Do not use when: Do not use for multi-month trends.  Produces: monthly income, monthly expenses, monthly net.

month.description: Month as YYYY-MM. Defaults to the current month.

function.name: finance_net_worth
function.description: Compute current net worth from finance accounts included in net-worth totals, summing posted transaction activity per account. Returns per-account balances grouped by currency. Includes excluded rows; pending rows are omitted. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks for current net worth or account balances. Do not use when: Do not use for transaction history or category spending.  Produces: account balances, net worth totals.

includeClosed.description: Whether to include closed accounts in the current balance totals.

function.name: finance_recent_transactions
function.description: List posted finance transactions in a bounded window, optionally scoped to one account, with category annotations where available. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks for recent transactions or spending evidence. Do not use when: Do not use for net worth or category aggregation.  Produces: transaction ids, transaction dates, merchant names, amounts.

accountId.description: Optional. Omit to include every account; set only to narrow to one account ID a finance tool returned.

from.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

to.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

limit.description: Maximum number of transactions to return, from 1 to 50.

function.name: finance_rule_create
function.description: Create an automation rule that files transactions whose description matches a pattern into a category. Names are unique per owner case-insensitively; a category must already exist (rules never create categories). Mode: write. Use when: The user wants a merchant or description to be filed automatically. Do not use when: Do not use to reclassify historical transactions; edit them instead.  Prerequisites: finance_categories (resolve the category the rule files into).

category.description: Category to file matches into, by name or id.

matchMode.description: How matchPattern is compared against a transaction description.

function.name: finance_rule_delete
function.description: Permanently delete an automation rule by name or id. Transactions it already filed keep their category. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: finance_rule_update
function.description: Update a rule by name or id, including repointing it at another category — the move a blocked category merge asks for. Omitted fields are left unchanged. Mode: write.

category.description: Repoint the rule at this category, by name or id.

function.name: finance_rules
function.description: List automation rules: description patterns that file matching transactions into a category. Each rule reports the category it currently files into. Mode: read-only. Use when: Before a category merge, or when the user asks what automations they have.  Produces: rule names, rule patterns, the category each rule files into.

function.name: finance_runway
function.description: Project weekly cash from liquid accounts (checking, savings, cash) using trailing recurring outflows plus an optional monthly budget allowance. Uses the user-selected forecast currency and posted, non-excluded ledger rows. Derived from current data on every call; nothing is stored. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks how long their cash will last or what their balance will look like. Do not use when: Do not use for current balances; use finance_accounts.  Produces: weekly cash projection, weekly recurring outflow.

monthlyBudgets.description: Optional monthly spending caps per category, in cents, used as the flat variable allowance.

projectionWeeks.description: Number of weeks to project, from 1 to 52.

asOf.description: Projection start date. Defaults to today.

function.name: finance_spending_by_category
function.description: Sum posted, non-excluded, non-transfer spending grouped by category and currency over a date range (defaults to the last 30 days through today). Each category row is reported in its own currency; mixed-currency values are never combined. Check truncated and warnings because results may omit categories beyond the requested limit. Mode: read-only.

from.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

to.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

limit.description: Maximum number of categories to return, from 1 to 50.

function.name: finance_tag_breakdown
function.description: Break posted, non-excluded spending down by each assigned tag with per-currency shares and a per-day average. Untagged transactions appear as (untagged); a co-tagged transaction counts under every tag. Computed from posted, non-excluded transactions in the range. Spending is every negative amount, so transfers between accounts are included. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks how spending splits across their own tags. Do not use when: Do not use for the ledger category breakdown; use finance_spending_by_category.  Produces: tag names, tag spending shares.

from.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

to.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

accountId.description: Stable account ID returned by finance_accounts.

tag.description: Restrict to transactions carrying this tag, given as a tag id or a tag name.

limit.description: Maximum tags to return, from 1 to 50.

function.name: finance_tag_merge
function.description: Move every assignment from one tag to another, then delete the emptied tag. Assignments the target already holds are not duplicated. Tags are owner-wide, so a merge affects every domain that uses them. Mode: write, confirmation required.

from.description: Tag to fold away, matched case-insensitively.

function.name: finance_tag_rename
function.description: Rename a tag (display name only), keeping its id and every assignment. Refuses with target_exists when another tag already holds the new name — merge is for that. Tags are owner-wide, so a rename shows wherever the tag is used. Mode: write.

function.name: finance_top_merchants
function.description: Rank merchants by total spending, optionally filtered by date range, account or tag. Computed from posted, non-excluded transactions in the range. Spending is every negative amount, so transfers between accounts are included. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks where their money goes or which merchants they spend the most at. Do not use when: Do not use for category totals; use finance_spending_by_category.  Produces: merchant names, merchant spending totals.

from.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

to.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

accountId.description: Stable account ID returned by finance_accounts.

tag.description: Restrict to transactions carrying this tag, given as a tag id or a tag name.

limit.description: Maximum merchants to return, from 1 to 50.

function.name: finance_transaction_delete
function.description: Hard-delete finance transactions by id (1–200). Requires iUnderstand: true — that flag is the confirmation contract and the server never elicits on top of it. Unknown ids come back in notFound, never as an error. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: Removing a synthetic, duplicate or bad-sync transaction by id. Do not use when: Do not guess ids; resolve them via finance_transaction_search first.  Prerequisites: finance_transaction_search (resolve the stable transaction id).

iUnderstand.description: Must be true. This flag is the confirmation contract; the server never elicits.

function.name: finance_transaction_move
function.description: Move owned transactions to another owned account while preserving transaction ids and links. Mode: write. Use when: Correct transactions filed under the wrong account. Do not use when: Do not use to alter transaction values or counterpart links.

function.name: finance_transaction_search
function.description: Search transactions by text across description, merchant, category and account names, with optional date range, account, tag, category-name and transaction-type filters. Text matching is case-insensitive and fuzzy. Includes pending and excluded transactions (flagged), newest posted date first, and pages with offset. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks to find specific transactions, e.g. "what did I pay Comcast". Do not use when: Use finance_recent_transactions for a plain recent-activity list.  Produces: transaction ids, transaction amounts, merchant names.

query.description: Case-insensitive, fuzzy text matched against transaction descriptions, merchant names, category names and account names.

from.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

to.description: Inclusive ISO calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in the user timezone.

accountId.description: Stable account ID returned by finance_accounts.

tag.description: Restrict to transactions carrying this tag, given as a tag id or a tag name.

transactionType.description: Restrict results to this transaction type.

limit.description: Maximum transactions to return, from 1 to 50.

offset.description: Number of matches to skip, for paging.

function.name: finance_transaction_upsert
function.description: Upsert a single finance transaction. Without externalId, identity is derived from postedOn, account, description, amountCents and currencyCode; when externalId is supplied, that provider identity is used. Unknown accounts are rejected, never auto-created. A rejected row returns reason and null id instead of failing the call. Mode: write. Use when: Pushing one sheet row or correcting a single transaction. Do not use when: Do not invent account labels; resolve them via finance_accounts first.  Prerequisites: finance_accounts (resolve the account id).

account.description: Sheet Bank label or a Hominem account id.

amountCents.description: Signed amount in cents; negative = outflow.

tags.description: Sheet Tags; comma-separated values also split.

pending.description: v1 has no pending state — pending rows are rejected loudly.

counterpartId.description: Other leg of an internal transfer: an owned transaction on a different account. The link is mirrored on both rows; invalid targets are rejected as invalid_counterpart.

function.name: finance_transactions_import
function.description: Batch upsert for backfills and daily deltas (max 1000 rows per call). Append adds or updates rows and returns row-level rejections. Replace deletes all of this user’s finance transactions before inserting, requires iUnderstand: true, and refuses the whole replace if any row is rejected. dryRun validates and reports the projected result without writing. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: Backfilling sheet history or pushing daily deltas. Do not use when: Do not use mode replace without explicit confirmation.  Prerequisites: finance_accounts (build the sheet-label map).

account.description: Sheet Bank label or a Hominem account id.

amountCents.description: Signed amount in cents; negative = outflow.

tags.description: Sheet Tags; comma-separated values also split.

pending.description: v1 has no pending state — pending rows are rejected loudly.

counterpartId.description: Other leg of an internal transfer: an owned transaction on a different account. The link is mirrored on both rows; invalid targets are rejected as invalid_counterpart.

transactions.description: Batch of sheet rows, in order, max 1000 per call.

iUnderstand.description: Explicit confirmation for mode: "replace", which wipes the store first.

function.name: forget_memory
function.description: Permanently deletes a saved memory. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: health_daily_summary
function.description: Returns daily aggregated health metrics (steps, distance, calories, elevation) from tracker samples and daily/hourly summaries. Mode: read-only.

function.name: health_recent_workouts
function.description: Lists recent workouts (runs, cycles, weights, yoga, etc.) with duration, calories, distance, and heart rate metrics. Mode: read-only.

function.name: health_sleep_summary
function.description: Lists recent sleep sessions with stage breakdowns (deep, light, REM, awake), total sleep duration, heart rate, and wake-up count. Mode: read-only.

function.name: invite_member
function.description: Invite another hominem user (by email) to collaborate on a collection as an editor or viewer. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: The user explicitly asks to invite a collaborator to a known collection. Do not use when: Do not invite without confirmation or a stable collection id.  Prerequisites: list_collections (resolve the stable collection id).  Produces: member id, invitation state.

collectionId.description: Stable collection id returned by a collection lookup or create operation.

email.description: Email address of the collaborator to invite.

function.name: leave_collection
function.description: Removes you from a collection someone else owns. Owners can't leave their own collection; use delete_collection instead. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: The user asks to stop collaborating on a collection they do not own. Do not use when: Do not use on a collection the user owns.  Prerequisites: list_collections (resolve the stable collection id).

function.name: list_collections
function.description: List collections you own or collaborate on, most recently created first. Mode: read-only.

function.name: list_memories
function.description: Lists the most recently saved memories about the user, newest first. Mode: read-only. Use when: A broad recent-memory review is requested or keyword search is not useful. Do not use when: Do not use as a substitute for current domain data such as trips or finances.  Produces: memory ids, memory content.

limit.description: Maximum memories to return, from 1 to 50.

function.name: list_pending_collection_invites
function.description: List pending invitations to collections for the caller. Mode: read-only.

function.name: media_item_history
function.description: Returns a media item's details and its full activity history (watches, listens, reads, etc.). Mode: read-only.

function.name: media_recent_activity
function.description: Lists recent media activity (watches, listens, reads, purchases) across all media types, newest first. Mode: read-only.

function.name: media_want_to_watch
function.description: Lists media items marked as want-to-watch, newest first. Mode: read-only.

function.name: music_purchase_history
function.description: Lists music purchases (iTunes, Amazon Music, etc.), newest first. Mode: read-only.

function.name: music_recent_plays
function.description: Lists recent music plays (listen activity), newest first, with track and artist names. Mode: read-only.

function.name: note_create
function.description: Saves a new note with an optional title. Mode: write. Use when: The user asks to write down, save or capture something as a note. Do not use when: Do not use for durable personal facts; use remember instead.  Produces: note id.

function.name: note_delete
function.description: Permanently deletes a note. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: A note id has been returned by note_list or note_get and the user asked to delete it. Do not use when: Do not invent a note id or delete before lookup and confirmation.  Prerequisites: note_list (resolve the stable note id).

function.name: note_get
function.description: Returns the full content of a note by id, or null if it does not exist. Mode: read-only. Use when: A note id has been returned by note_list, semantic_search or note_create. Do not use when: Do not invent a note id.  Prerequisites: note_list (resolve the stable note id).

function.name: note_list
function.description: Lists the user's notes, most recently updated first, optionally filtered by a keyword matched against titles and content. Returns summaries; use note_get for the full body. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks about their notes or wants to find one by keyword. Do not use when: Do not use for remembered personal facts; use search_memories instead.  Produces: note ids, note titles, note excerpts.

query.description: Optional keyword matched against note titles and content.

function.name: note_update
function.description: Replaces a note's title and/or content. Returns null if the note does not exist. Mode: write. Use when: A note id has been returned by note_list or note_get. Do not use when: Do not invent a note id.  Prerequisites: note_list (resolve the stable note id).

id.description: Stable note id returned by note_list or note_create.

function.name: people_lookup
function.description: Searches people by name or alias and returns a summary with contact info, organizations, and tags. Mode: read-only. Use when: A person must be resolved by name or alias before requesting person-specific data. Do not use when: Do not guess a person id or use this for general relationship questions.  Produces: person ids, person names, contact summaries.

query.description: Person name, alias, or identifying phrase.

function.name: person_create
function.description: Adds a person to the address book with an optional primary email. Call people_lookup first so the same person is not added twice. Mode: write. Use when: The user asks to add someone and people_lookup found no match. Do not use when: Do not create a person that people_lookup already returns.  Prerequisites: people_lookup (avoid creating a duplicate).  Produces: person id.

parameters.description: A person to add to the address book.

function.name: person_timeline
function.description: A person’s activity across identity, travel, and relationships, newest first. Requires people, travel, and social read access. Mode: read-only. Use when: A resolved person id is available and the user asks for that person's cross-domain timeline. Do not use when: Do not call before people_lookup has identified a person id.  Prerequisites: people_lookup (requires a stable person id).  Produces: person timeline, related trips, relationships.

personId.description: Stable person id returned by people_lookup.

function.name: person_update
function.description: Changes a person's display name and/or primary email. Returns null if the person does not exist. Mode: write. Use when: A person id has been returned by people_lookup. Do not use when: Do not invent a person id.  Prerequisites: people_lookup (resolve the stable person id).

personId.description: Stable person id returned by people_lookup or person_create.

email.description: Sets the person's primary email; null removes it.

function.name: place_residence_create
function.description: Records a place the person has lived and its lived-in periods. Mode: write.

function.name: place_residence_delete
function.description: Deletes a residence history record after explicit confirmation. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: place_residence_get
function.description: Gets a lived-in history record by UUID. Mode: read-only.

function.name: place_residence_list
function.description: Lists places the person has lived and their recorded periods. Mode: read-only.

function.name: place_residence_update
function.description: Replaces recorded lived-in periods and/or notes. Mode: write.

function.name: place_visit_history
function.description: Lists visits to places (restaurants, venues, addresses), newest first, with the visited place's name and address. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks which restaurants, venues, or addresses they visited. Do not use when: Do not use to answer trip-history questions when no place visit is requested.  Produces: place ids, place names, visit dates.

function.name: possession_bulk_upsert
function.description: Upserts up to 100 possessions keyed on externalId. Not atomic: each item succeeds or fails on its own and the per-item results say which, so a single bad row never blocks the rest. Mode: write. Use when: Importing many items at once, e.g. the sheet backlog.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).  Produces: id.

function.name: possession_create
function.description: Creates a possession. Prices are integer cents with a 3-letter currencyCode. To place it, pass a containerId from container_list. Search with possession_list first to avoid duplicates. Mode: write.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).  Produces: id.

function.name: possession_delete
function.description: Permanently deletes a possession. Prefer possession_update with isArchived=true or status=disposed to keep history. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: The user explicitly wants the record gone. Do not use when: Do not delete before lookup and confirmation; archive instead when unsure.  Prerequisites: possession_list (resolve the stable possession id (search by name, brand or model)).

function.name: possession_get
function.description: Returns one possession by id, or null if it does not exist. Mode: read-only. Use when: A possession id has been returned by possession_list. Do not use when: Do not invent a possession id.  Prerequisites: possession_list (resolve the stable possession id (search by name, brand or model)).

function.name: possession_history
function.description: Returns the append-only audit log for one possession, newest first: creations, updates, moves, status changes, and archivals with the fields that changed. Mode: read-only. Use when: Asking "what changed on X" or auditing an item. Do not use when: Do not invent a possession id.  Prerequisites: possession_list (resolve the stable possession id (search by name, brand or model)).

function.name: possession_list
function.description: Lists the user's possessions, newest first. Filter by status (wishlist, planned, ordered, delivered, owned, in_use, retired, disposed, donated, sold), archived flag, containerId, category, and a text query matching name, brand or model — use these instead of listing everything and filtering client-side. Returns up to 100 per call; pass offset to page further. Archived items are included unless archived=false. Mode: read-only. Use when: Finding an item, browsing a category, or resolving a possession id.  Prerequisites: container_list (filter by container (containerId)).  Produces: id.

function.name: possession_move
function.description: Moves up to 50 possessions into a container, or out of any container when containerId is null. Returns the ids that moved and the ids that were not found. Mode: write. Use when: Packing, unpacking or relocating several items at once.  Prerequisites: possession_list (resolve the stable possession id (search by name, brand or model)); container_list (resolve the stable container id).

function.name: possession_summary
function.description: Inventory overview of non-archived possessions: total count, how many are not in any container, counts by status and top categories, and total purchase/sell value for up to 20 currencies (most-used first); currenciesOmitted says how many more were left out. Mode: read-only. Use when: Questions like "how much stuff do I own" or "what is it all worth".

function.name: possession_update
function.description: Updates fields on a possession. Only provided fields change; metadata keys are merged, not replaced. Returns null if the possession does not exist. Use isArchived to archive, status to move it through the lifecycle. Mode: write. Use when: A possession id has been returned by possession_list or possession_get. Do not use when: Do not invent a possession id.  Prerequisites: possession_list (resolve the stable possession id (search by name, brand or model)).

function.name: possession_upsert
function.description: Creates a possession or updates the one already carrying externalId (e.g. ITM-023). Returns the id and whether the row was created. Re-running with the same input never duplicates: it is the primitive for imports and sync. Mode: write. Use when: Importing or syncing an item that has a stable external id.  Prerequisites: container_list (resolve the stable container id).  Produces: id.

function.name: possession_validate
function.description: Integrity audit replacing manual sheet audits: unplaced live items, items missing weight, moveAction tokens matching no container, retired statuses that are not archived, archived items still in a container, zero prices, prices without currency, and unknown vessel groups. Returns findings with severity error or warning, paginated with limit/offset while total says how many exist. Mode: read-only. Use when: Scheduled audits or after an import to catch data problems.

function.name: remember
function.description: Saves a durable fact, preference, or piece of personal context as a memory. Call this immediately when the user asks to be remembered something, or when a lasting fact about them surfaces naturally in conversation — no confirmation needed before saving. Each call saves exactly one distinct fact: if the user mentions several facts, make one call per fact. Never save the same fact more than once or under multiple titles — an identical fact already in memory is returned as-is instead of being saved again. Mode: write. Use when: The user explicitly asks to remember something or states a durable preference. Do not use when: Do not save transient instructions, one-off plans, or facts about other people. Things the user needs to do, deadlines, appointments and reminders are tasks: use task_create.  Produces: memory id, saved memory content.

content.description: One durable fact or preference about the user.

title.description: Optional short title for the memory.

function.name: remove_collection_item
function.description: Remove an entity from a collection. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: The user explicitly asks to remove a known entity from a collection. Do not use when: Do not remove items without confirmation or stable collection and entity ids.  Prerequisites: list_collections (resolve the stable collection id).  Produces: removed state.

function.name: remove_member
function.description: Removes a member or pending invite from a collection you own. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: The owner explicitly asks to remove a collaborator or revoke an invite. Do not use when: Do not invent member ids; read them from collection_detail.  Prerequisites: collection_detail (resolve the member id).

function.name: search_memories
function.description: Searches saved memories by keyword. Call this before answering questions that plausibly depend on remembered personal context, rather than assuming none exists. If no keyword match is found, returns the full recent memory list instead so nothing is missed. Mode: read-only. Use when: A response depends on remembered personal context and a keyword search is appropriate. Do not use when: Do not use as a substitute for current domain data such as trips or finances.  Produces: memory ids, memory content.

query.description: Keywords describing the remembered fact or preference.

limit.description: Maximum matching memories to return, from 1 to 50.

function.name: semantic_search
function.description: Finds notes whose meaning is closest to a natural-language query, even when they share no keywords with it. Only notes that have finished indexing appear; a note created moments ago may not be searchable yet, so fall back to note_list for very recent notes. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user describes what a note was about but keyword search is unlikely to match. Do not use when: Use note_list when the user gives an exact keyword or title.  Produces: note ids, similarity scores.

query.description: Natural-language description of what to find; matches by meaning, not keywords.

function.name: social_conversation_activity
function.description: Rank social conversations by message volume in a bounded date range, with platform, title, and latest message time. Message counts only — no message content. Mode: read-only.

function.name: social_engagement_summary
function.description: Summarize social engagement (likes, comments, reactions) counts by platform and type over a bounded date range. Counts only — no message or comment content. Mode: read-only.

function.name: tag_entity
function.description: Tags an owned person, venue place, possession, note, or travel entity with a named tag. Travel Place and Residence are distinct from venue places. Mode: write.

function.name: task_batch_create
function.description: Creates one or more task-list groups (each with subtasks) and/or standalone tasks in a single call. Mode: write.

function.name: task_complete
function.description: Marks a task as completed or pending. Mode: write. Use when: The user says a task is done or asks to reopen it. Resolve a loose reference such as "it" or "the gym thing" by listing tasks and matching titles. Do not use when: The user wants a task gone, which is task_delete. Completing it is not a way to remove it.  Prerequisites: task_list (resolve the stable task id).

function.name: task_create
function.description: Creates a standalone task, optionally assigning participants or nesting it under a parent task list. Use task_batch_create to create a task list with subtasks. Mode: write. Use when: The user says they need or want to do something, mentions a deadline or appointment, or asks to be reminded, even if they never say "add a task". Do not use when: Do not use for a durable fact or preference about the user; use remember for those.

function.name: task_delete
function.description: Deletes a task. If it is a task list, its child tasks are deleted too. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: The user asked to delete or get rid of a task and a matching task id has been returned by task_list. Resolve a loose reference such as "it" or "the gym thing" by listing tasks and matching titles. Never call it before task_list has returned the task, and never with a guessed id. If task_list returns more than one task the words the user used could refer to (for example "passport" matching both "Renew passport" and "Passport photo appointment"), do not pick one and do not call this tool: ask which one they mean. Only once exactly one task matches, call this tool with that task's id: the app shows the user an approval prompt for it, so do not ask "do you want me to delete it?" in text first. Do not use when: Do not invent a task id. If several tasks could be the one the user means, ask which before calling; a guess is wrong even though the app asks for approval.  Prerequisites: task_list (resolve the stable task id).

function.name: task_detail
function.description: Returns a task or task list by id, including its children (if a list) and assigned participants. Mode: read-only.

function.name: task_list
function.description: Lists top-level tasks and task lists for the authenticated user. Supports filtering by status, priority, due date range (dueBefore/dueAfter), and a title text search (query) — use these instead of listing everything and filtering client-side, e.g. for "what is due today" or "what is overdue". Omit every filter the user did not ask for: with none it returns up to 100 tasks, and an unneeded filter silently hides the rest. Mode: read-only.

status.description: Only set when the user asked specifically for pending or for completed tasks. Leave out otherwise.

query.description: A keyword from the title of the task the user means ("gym", "passport"). Leave out to list everything.

function.name: task_update
function.description: Updates fields on a task (title, description, priority, due date, scheduling, location), optionally replacing its participants. Mode: write. Use when: A matching task id has been returned by task_list. Resolve a loose reference such as "it" or "the gym thing" by listing tasks and matching titles. Do not use when: Do not invent a task id.  Prerequisites: task_list (resolve the stable task id).

function.name: travel_airport_get
function.description: Gets the resolved airport or station by code, including OurAirports and travel curation provenance. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks what an endpoint code resolves to. Do not use when: they ask about venues. Prerequisites: provide a code. Produces: reference and curation state for that code. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_airport_list
function.description: Searches the working set by default, or the shared OurAirports reference data by code, name, city, or country when a query is supplied. Scheduled-service airports rank first, with smaller fields searchable. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user needs to select an airport or inspect a used endpoint. Prerequisites: none. Produces: reference provenance, curation, and endpoint codes. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_airport_update
function.description: Sets travel-specific airport curation by code. Reference data stays read-only. For codes outside the reference dataset, provide the full station fields to add a standalone endpoint. Mode: write. Prerequisites: use an existing Place UUID target by name in servesPlace. Produces: the merged airport view. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_booking_lookup
function.description: Searches transport and lodging bookings by exact or partial booking reference. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user provides a travel booking reference. Do not use when: they ask for all legs or stays. Prerequisites: booking reference. Produces: matching transport and stay ids. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_countries
function.description: Returns places grouped by country with all recorded presence evidence: itinerary stops, connected-flight layovers, visits, and residence periods. A place can have multiple evidence types. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks where they have been, lived, stopped, or had a layover, or asks for country totals. Do not treat a layover as a destination stop or collapse multiple evidence types. Prerequisites: none. Produces: country identities, places, evidence types, dates, and source record IDs. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_distance
function.description: Calculates haversine distance between two registered airports and resolves their served places. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks how far a route is. Do not use when: they ask for recorded transport legs or trip totals. Prerequisites: airport codes. Produces: airport ids and resolved place names. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_entity_history
function.description: Reads append-only changes for one travel entity, including deleted entities. Mode: read-only. Use when: the caller asks what changed. Do not use when: the current entity snapshot is enough. Prerequisites: provide entity type and stable id. Produces: audit event ids, operations, changed fields, snapshots, and timestamps. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_export
function.description: Exports all travel entities in native format, including residences and airport curation. Mode: read-only. Use when: the caller needs a backup or parity diff. Do not use when: records need to be imported or changed. Prerequisites: none. Produces: the complete travel dataset. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_idea_create
function.description: Creates or returns an existing travel idea by its natural key. Mode: write. Use when: a resolved travel idea needs to be recorded. Do not use when: the entity already exists and needs correction; use its update tool. Prerequisites: resolve referenced UUIDs first. Produces: the idea UUID. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_idea_delete
function.description: Deletes an unused travel idea after explicit confirmation. Mode: write. Use when: a resolved entity should be removed. Do not use when: the entity remains referenced; merge or repoint first. Prerequisites: id and iUnderstand=true. Produces: deleted snapshot or in-use refusal. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: travel_idea_list
function.description: Lists travel ideas by status and type. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks about recorded travel ideas. Do not use when: they ask for the full travel wish list. Prerequisites: none. Produces: idea UUIDs. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_idea_update
function.description: Updates an owned travel idea with optimistic concurrency. Mode: write. Use when: a matching id has been resolved. Do not use when: the entity should be removed; use its delete tool. Prerequisites: provide the stable id. Produces: the updated entity and change counters. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_import
function.description: Batch upsert the seven travel entities from sheet-shaped rows. Append is idempotent; replace clears this user’s travel records first and requires explicit confirmation. dryRun validates and projects counts without writing. Mode: write, confirmation required. Use when: Import or reconcile a batch of travel records. Do not use when: Do not use replace without explicit confirmation or bypass row rejections.

function.name: travel_insights
function.description: Ranks places, countries, routes, stays, travel years, and home periods from recorded travel data. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks for travel patterns or a next-trip summary. Do not use when: they ask for a complete event-by-event timeline. Prerequisites: none. Produces: place, journey, leg, and residence references. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_journey_clone
function.description: Creates a draft copy of a journey and shifts its dated records, clearing booking references. Mode: write. Use when: planning a similar trip. Do not use when: editing the original journey. Prerequisites: source journey id. Produces: the new journey and copied counts. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_journey_create
function.description: Creates or returns an existing travel journey by its natural key. Mode: write. Use when: a resolved travel journey needs to be recorded. Do not use when: the entity already exists and needs correction; use its update tool. Prerequisites: resolve referenced UUIDs first. Produces: the journey UUID. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_journey_delete
function.description: Deletes an owned travel journey after explicit confirmation. Mode: write. Use when: the caller has reviewed the entity and provided iUnderstand=true. Do not use when: references remain; resolve them first. Prerequisites: stable id and explicit confirmation. Produces: deleted snapshot or named refusal. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: travel_journey_get
function.description: Returns a complete journey dossier with stops, legs, resolved airports, distances, and stays. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks about one journey. Do not use when: a list or aggregate answers the question. Prerequisites: identify by UUID. Produces: journey, segment, transport, airport, and stay ids. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_journey_list
function.description: Lists journeys with derived stop summaries and filters. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks for trips, journeys, or a date range. Do not use when: the user asks only for legacy calendar trips; use trip_history. Prerequisites: none. Produces: journey UUIDs. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_journey_save
function.description: Atomically upserts a journey and its segments, transport, and stays. Mode: write. Use when: recording a complete trip dossier. Do not use when: correcting one field on an existing entity. Prerequisites: resolve all place, airport, and journey references. Produces: per-section change counters. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_journey_update
function.description: Updates an owned travel journey with optimistic concurrency. Mode: write. Use when: a matching id has been resolved. Do not use when: the entity should be removed; use its delete tool. Prerequisites: provide the stable id. Produces: the updated entity and change counters. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_place_create
function.description: Creates a new canonical Place and its travel relationship. Mode: write. Use when: this location is not already saved as a Place. Do not use when: an existing Place should be marked for travel; use travel_place_update with its UUID. Prerequisites: check place search first. Produces: the Place UUID. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_place_delete
function.description: Deletes an unused travel place after explicit confirmation. Mode: write. Use when: a resolved entity should be removed. Do not use when: the entity remains referenced; merge or repoint first. Prerequisites: id and iUnderstand=true. Produces: deleted snapshot or in-use refusal. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: travel_place_get
function.description: Returns one travel place with visit history, residence periods, and derived relationships. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks if or when they visited or lived in a destination. Do not use when: they ask about a restaurant, venue, or address visit. Prerequisites: identify by UUID. Produces: place, journey, segment, and residence ids. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_place_list
function.description: Lists canonical travel places with derived visit and residence relationships. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks about destinations, countries, or visited and wanted places. Do not use when: they ask about venues or restaurants; use place_visit_history. Prerequisites: none. Produces: travel place UUIDs. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_place_merge
function.description: Moves segment and residence references to a canonical travel place, then removes the source place. Mode: write. Use when: the operator confirms duplicate place identity. Do not use when: records are merely similar. Prerequisites: source and destination ids and iUnderstand=true. Produces: deleted snapshot and repointed count. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: travel_place_refresh
function.description: Compares or explicitly refreshes stored place status and visit dates from segments. Mode: write. Use when: the operator requests a place reconciliation. Do not use when: validating discrepancies only. Prerequisites: review the full dry-run diff first. Produces: all changed fields. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_place_update
function.description: Updates an owned travel place with optimistic concurrency. Mode: write. Use when: a matching id has been resolved. Do not use when: the entity should be removed; use its delete tool. Prerequisites: provide the stable id. Produces: the updated entity and change counters. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_search
function.description: Searches journey names and notes, places, stays, carriers, booking references, and ideas. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user gives a text query across travel records. Do not use when: a precise entity filter is available. Prerequisites: a search query. Produces: matching UUIDs grouped by entity type. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_segment_create
function.description: Creates or returns an existing travel segment by its natural key. Mode: write. Use when: a resolved travel segment needs to be recorded. Do not use when: the entity already exists and needs correction; use its update tool. Prerequisites: resolve referenced UUIDs first. Produces: the segment UUID. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_segment_delete
function.description: Deletes an owned travel segment after explicit confirmation. Mode: write. Use when: the caller has reviewed the entity and provided iUnderstand=true. Do not use when: references remain; resolve them first. Prerequisites: stable id and explicit confirmation. Produces: deleted snapshot or named refusal. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: travel_segment_get
function.description: Returns one stop with its journey, arrival and departure legs, and stays. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks about a particular stop. Do not use when: they mean a restaurant or venue visit. Prerequisites: identify by UUID. Produces: segment, journey, leg, and stay ids. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_segment_list
function.description: Lists journey stops with optional journey, place, and date filters. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks which places a journey includes or when a stop occurred. Do not use when: the full journey dossier is needed. Prerequisites: none. Produces: segment and journey ids. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_segment_merge
function.description: Merges one stop into another in the same journey, repointing stays and transport links. Mode: write. Use when: two stops are confirmed duplicates. Do not use when: they represent distinct visits. Prerequisites: both segment ids and iUnderstand=true. Produces: survivor and deleted snapshot. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: travel_segment_reorder
function.description: Atomically assigns segment sequence values for a complete journey order. Mode: write. Use when: the user explicitly changes stop order. Do not use when: changing only one stop field. Prerequisites: complete ordered segment id list. Produces: the new sequence. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_segment_update
function.description: Updates an owned travel segment with optimistic concurrency. Mode: write. Use when: a matching id has been resolved. Do not use when: the entity should be removed; use its delete tool. Prerequisites: provide the stable id. Produces: the updated entity and change counters. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_stats
function.description: Summarizes segment-derived places, countries, journeys, legs, and distances. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks for travel totals or records by year. Do not use when: they ask for a detailed timeline. Prerequisites: none. Produces: journey and place UUIDs for the returned trip summaries. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_stay_create
function.description: Creates or returns an existing travel stay by its natural key. Mode: write. Use when: a resolved travel stay needs to be recorded. Do not use when: the entity already exists and needs correction; use its update tool. Prerequisites: resolve referenced UUIDs first. Produces: the stay UUID. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_stay_delete
function.description: Deletes an owned travel stay after explicit confirmation. Mode: write. Use when: the caller has reviewed the entity and provided iUnderstand=true. Do not use when: references remain; resolve them first. Prerequisites: stable id and explicit confirmation. Produces: deleted snapshot or named refusal. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: travel_stay_get
function.description: Gets one travel stay by UUID. Mode: read-only. Use when: one resolved stay is needed. Do not use when: a collection is requested. Prerequisites: stable entity UUID. Produces: the stay snapshot. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_stay_list
function.description: Lists lodging records with optional city, journey, segment, and evidence filters. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks where they stayed or about lodging plans. Do not use when: they ask about flight or rail bookings. Prerequisites: none. Produces: stay, journey, and segment ids. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_stay_update
function.description: Updates an owned travel stay with optimistic concurrency. Mode: write. Use when: a matching id has been resolved. Do not use when: the entity should be removed; use its delete tool. Prerequisites: provide the stable id. Produces: the updated entity and change counters. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_timeline
function.description: Interleaves dated journey stops with home gaps labelled from Residence periods. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks when trips happened or when they were home. Do not use when: they need aggregate counts only. Prerequisites: none. Produces: journey, segment, and residence references. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_transport_create
function.description: Creates or returns an existing travel transport by its natural key. Mode: write. Use when: a resolved travel transport needs to be recorded. Do not use when: the entity already exists and needs correction; use its update tool. Prerequisites: resolve referenced UUIDs first. Produces: the transport UUID. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_transport_delete
function.description: Deletes an owned travel transport after explicit confirmation. Mode: write. Use when: the caller has reviewed the entity and provided iUnderstand=true. Do not use when: references remain; resolve them first. Prerequisites: stable id and explicit confirmation. Produces: deleted snapshot or named refusal. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: travel_transport_get
function.description: Gets one travel transport by UUID. Mode: read-only. Use when: one resolved transport is needed. Do not use when: a collection is requested. Prerequisites: stable entity UUID. Produces: the transport snapshot. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_transport_list
function.description: Lists flights and rail legs with airport and served-place resolution. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks about flights, trains, carriers, routes, dates, or bookings. Do not use when: they ask about lodging. Prerequisites: none. Produces: transport, journey, and airport codes. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_transport_update
function.description: Updates an owned travel transport with optimistic concurrency. Mode: write. Use when: a matching id has been resolved. Do not use when: the entity should be removed; use its delete tool. Prerequisites: provide the stable id. Produces: the updated entity and change counters. Mode: write.

function.name: travel_unresolved
function.description: Combines thin-evidence stays, open admin ideas, and integrity counts. Mode: read-only. Use when: the operator asks what travel records need triage. Do not use when: they ask for one entity or a broad text search. Prerequisites: none. Produces: stay and idea ids with validation counts. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_validate
function.description: Reports travel data integrity checks and offending entity references without changing records. Mode: read-only. Use when: the operator asks about consistency, import quality, or unresolved discrepancies. Do not use when: they ask to repair data. Prerequisites: none. Produces: entity UUIDs for findings. Mode: read-only.

function.name: travel_wishlist
function.description: Returns wanted places, unlinked wishlist stays, and open experience ideas in separate sections. Mode: read-only. Use when: the user asks what travel plans or ideas are on their wish list. Do not use when: they ask for completed visits. Prerequisites: none. Produces: place, stay, and idea ids. Mode: read-only.

function.name: trip_history
function.description: Lists past and upcoming trips, newest first, with attendee names. Mode: read-only. Use when: The user asks about past or upcoming trips, destinations, dates, or attendees. Do not use when: Do not use for restaurant or venue visits without a travel question.  Produces: trip ids, trip dates, trip destinations, attendee names.

from.description: Inclusive start date in the user data timezone.

to.description: Inclusive end date in the user data timezone.

function.name: untag_entity
function.description: Removes a tag from an owned person, venue place, possession, note, or travel entity, including a Residence. Mode: write, confirmation required.

function.name: update_collection
function.description: Renames a collection or changes its description or visibility. Only the owner can update it; returns null if it doesn't exist or isn't yours. Mode: write. Use when: The user asks to rename or change a collection they own. Do not use when: Do not invent a collection id.  Prerequisites: list_collections (resolve the stable collection id).

function.name: update_member_role
function.description: Switches a collection member between editor and viewer. Only the owner can do this; returns null if the collection or member isn't found. Mode: write. Use when: The owner asks to change what a collaborator can do. Do not use when: Do not invent member ids; read them from collection_detail.  Prerequisites: collection_detail (resolve the member id).

function.name: vessel_weight_report
function.description: Packing report replacing the sheet weights tab: per vessel the summed item weights, case tare, total, airline limit, notes, and whether it is over the limit, plus cabin/checked group rollups. An item counts toward its moveAction vessel first, else its outermost container. Tokens matching no container are still summed but flagged unknownVessel — investigate those before trusting the totals. Mode: read-only. Use when: Questions like "are my bags overweight" or "what is in box N".
